In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the incremental cost-effectiveness of LS testing for CRC in the Netherlands is uncertain.
LS testing is likely to be effective and cost-effective in the Netherlands, but not necessarily in other settings or health-care systems.
routine testing is likely to be more cost-effective relative to targeted testing in the Dutch setting, but it remains to be seen whether the same conclusion would apply to other settings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cost-effectiveness of genetic testing is highly sensitive to the epidemiologic context and that the epidemiologic assumptions underpinning cost-effectiveness conclusions must be made explicit and examined.
the cost effectiveness of universal screening for LS is highly sensitive to assumptions about the effectiveness of screening and the cost of testing.
routine testing for Lynch syndrome is cost-effective, and we should be testing all patients with colorectal cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the epidemiology of disease incidence and disease progression matters.
